issues.legal_issue: A court must resolve foundational questions about a plaintiff’s ability to bring a representative suit and the suit’s capacity to proceed as an ordinary suit before deciding the merits.
material_facts: A registered society claimed that land had been acquired for it through a branch and challenged a later sale of that land.
The society sought permission to prosecute the suit in a representative capacity under Order I Rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

The lower courts did not determine whether a juristic person could invoke that rule, whether the pleaded facts and reliefs met its requirements, or whether the suit could proceed as an ordinary suit concerning ownership of the land.
The objection had not been pressed by the defendant, but the Supreme Court considered the unresolved jurisdictional issue fundamental.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the judgments and decrees below were set aside, and the suit was remanded to the trial court to decide the identified threshold questions and then dispose of the suit according to law. The Supreme Court expressed no view on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: An issue going to the root of a court’s jurisdiction must be tried at any stage once it is brought to the court’s attention. Under Order I Rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court must consider whether a juristic person is a “person” entitled to sue representatively, whether the pleaded facts and reliefs satisfy the rule’s representative requirements for relief benefiting the public, and, if not, whether the suit can proceed as an ordinary suit for relief in the plaintiff’s personal capacity. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.civil_suit_claimed_as_representative: The plaintiff pursued a civil suit on the basis that it was brought in a representative capacity.
predicates.plaintiff_is_juristic_entity: The plaintiff was an organization recognized as a legal entity rather than a natural person.
predicates.threshold_suit_capacity_questions_unreso: The courts had not determined whether the plaintiff could sue representatively, whether the suit met the requirements for representative relief, or whether it could proceed as an ordinary suit.

issues.definition: When a civil suit is claimed to be representative, the plaintiff is a juristic entity, and the suit’s threshold capacity questions remain unresolved, the case is set aside and remanded for those questions to be determined.
